notes: The Daya Bay official experiment site (dayabay.ihep.ac.cn) timed out on every WebFetch attempt this session; this record relies on the INSPIRE experiment record, the 2012 discovery paper (arXiv:1203.1669), the detector paper (arXiv:1309.1557), and Wikipedia (used only for the pointer-level facts noted per-field).

This facility record covers the three underground experimental halls (Daya Bay near, Ling Ao near, far hall) as one reactor-neutrino site complex; no source fetched this session gives distinct, separately-sourced coordinates for the individual halls (see site:daya-bay-experimental-halls note).

summary.plain: A set of underground experimental halls near the Daya Bay and Ling Ao nuclear power plants in Guangdong, China, built to catch antineutrinos streaming out of the reactors.
summary.technical: Reactor-neutrino site hosting three underground experimental halls (two near halls and one far hall) at baselines of 470 m, 576 m and 1648 m from six 2.9 GW_th reactor cores at the Daya Bay and Ling Ao nuclear power complexes, Guangdong, China.
